VERDICT 1: REJECT
The first solution incorrectly double-counts the handshakes due to misunderstanding the condition that sorcerers do not shake hands with each other. It mistakenly adds all 60 handshakes made by the witches along with 51 (which is overstated due to improper adjustment for non-reciprocal handshakes among sorcerers), leading to an incorrect total.

VERDICT 2: REJECT
The second solution overlooks the fact that each of the 10 sorcerers shakes hands with all 6 witches, resulting in a total of 60 handshakes, not just 60 for the witches. This approach fails to consider the unique handshakes involving the sorcerers themselves.

VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
The third solution correctly addresses the problem by considering that each witch shakes hands with each of the 10 sorcerers exactly once, yielding 60 handshakes involving witches. Similarly, each sorcerer shakes hands with each of the 6 witches once, also resulting in 60 handshakes involving sorcerers. The division by 2 accounts for the fact that each handshake involves one witch and one sorcerer, avoiding double-counting. The accurate total is indeed 30 handshakes.
